questions.prompt: A planar serial arm has q₁=30° and relative q₂=40°. What is link 2 orientation in the base frame?
questions.explanation: The second orientation accumulates both relative joint rotations: 30°+40°=70°. The 40° is the elbow reading alone, 10° wrongly subtracts, and 30° forgets the elbow.

questions.prompt: If joint 1 rotates while relative joint 2 stays fixed, does link 2 base orientation change?
options: No: q₂ alone fixes its base orientation, whatever q₁ is.
Only if q₂ is changed at the same time as q₁.
Yes: link 2 is carried along, its orientation is q₁+q₂.
Yes, but only once q₁ exceeds 90° in magnitude.
questions.explanation: Link 2 is attached to link 1, so its base orientation is q₁+q₂.

questions.prompt: l₁=1.5, l₂=0.5, q₁=π/2, q₂=π/2. Give endpoint x.
l₁=1.5, l₂=0.5, q₁=π/6, q₂=π/3. Give endpoint y.
questions.explanation: The second link has world angle π/6+π/3=π/2: y=1.5sin(π/6)+0.5sin(π/2)=0.75+0.5=1.25.

questions.skillLabel: Solve the planar inverse by the law of cosines
questions.prompt: An arm has l₁=0.5 m, l₂=0.35 m and its tip is at (0.6, 0.45) m. Of the two joint solutions, take the one with q₂>0 (the mirrored elbow). Give q₁ in degrees.
questions.explanation: r²=0.5625, so cos q₂=(r²−l₁²−l₂²)/(2l₁l₂)=0.1900/0.35=0.5429 and q₂=+57.12°. Then q₁=atan2(y,x)−atan2(l₂ sin q₂, l₁+l₂ cos q₂)=36.87°−atan2(0.2939,0.6900)=36.87°−23.07°=13.80°. Substituting (13.80°, 57.12°) into the forward map returns (0.6, 0.45) m, as the other solution (59.94°, −57.12°) does.

questions.skillLabel: Workspace of an n-link planar chain
questions.prompt: Which 3-link planar chain (lengths in m, unrestricted joints) cannot reach points close to its base, i.e. has a hole in its workspace?
questions.explanation: The inner radius is max(0, 2·l_max − Σl). (0.5,0.4,0.3): 1.0−1.2<0, no hole. (0.6,0.6,0.6): 1.2−1.8<0, no hole. (0.9,0.25,0.15): 1.8−1.3=0.5>0, so points within 0.5 m of the base are unreachable. (0.4,0.3,0.3): 0.8−1.0<0, no hole. A hole appears only when one link is longer than the sum of the others.

questions.skillLabel: Noise amplification when estimating link lengths
questions.prompt: To estimate l₁ and l₂ you command q=(0, 15°) once and measure the tip with independent noise of 1 mm standard deviation in x and y. Using the exact 2×2 linear model, what is the standard deviation (mm) of the estimate of l₁?
questions.explanation: The model is [x;y]=[[cos q₁, cos(q₁+q₂)],[sin q₁, sin(q₁+q₂)]]·[l₁;l₂], here A=[[1,cos15°],[0,sin15°]]. Cov=σ²(AᵀA)⁻¹, whose diagonal gives 1/sin15°=3.86 mm for each length. The small singular value √(1−cos15°)=0.185 of A amplifies noise; at q₂=90° the same noise would give 1 mm.
